titleInfo.title: Herrad von Landsberg: Hortus Deliciarum. Copy
Herrad of Landsberg: Garden of delights. Copy
Herrad von Hohenburg: Hortus Deliciarum. Copy

mods.abstract: Original destroyed in 1870; copies only now exist
note: general: The illustrated encyclopedia was compiled by Herrad von Landsberg, Abbess of Hohenbourg, Alsace. The only copy was held in the municipal library of Strasbourg, but was destroyed by fire in the bombardment of the city in 1870. Christian Moritz Engelhardt copied miniatures for his 1818 publication of the Hortus. The manuscript had also been lent to the French antiquary Comte Auguste de Bastard d'Estang, who had notes on the text and some colored copies made of the illustrations 1832-1869. The contents of the manuscript are as follows: ff.2-68, Old Testament narrative and commentary (47 pages with miniatures and diagrams); ff.80v-133v, ancestry of Christ and incarnation, gospel narrative and commentary to the Last Supper (37 pages with miniatures); ff.138-167, gospel narrative and commentary, betrayal to ascension (15 pages with miniatures); ff.167v-199, Pentecost and acts of the apostles (10 pages with miniatures, 1 diagram); ff.199v-222, virtues and vices, Solomonic texts (17 pages with miniatures, including Psychomachia cycle, ff.199v-204); ff.222v-240v, texts dealing with the Church and society (6 pages with miniatures); ff.241-263v, escatological texts (20 pages with miniatures); ff.322v-324, songs about Hohenbourg (double page miniatures of the monastery).
